articles.title: Knicks' honeymoon phase over already? Behind the champs' slow start
articles.summary: The Knicks are just the third defending champion in NBA history to begin the ensuing season with three consecutive losses. It didn't end well for the previou...
articles.body:
You might say that Mike Brown saw this coming.

After a summer spent enjoying the spoils of helming the first New York Knicks team to win an NBA championship since the Nixon administration, the first time Brown sat down at a podium to discuss what might lay ahead in the 2026-27 campaign, the Knicks head coach repeatedly emphasized the need for his team to adhere to its established competitive standard. For his players to avoid any slippage in their day-to-day habits. For every member of the roster and staff to remain laser-focused on, and energetic in pursuit of, the process of putting themselves in position to compete for another championship.

Because, the coach predicted, the hardest work was just starting.

"You know, a lot of people tend to shy away from adversity — especially early on, because, you know, you get scrutinized, and sometimes it can be tough dealing with that," Brown said at the Knicks' media day session in September . "I actually yearn for it. I yearn for it early. Because I want to make sure that not only myself, but we as a group can handle it."

Well, Coach, I've got good news and bad news, and they're both the same thing. That early adversity you ordered? It has officially arrived.

After losing to the Philadelphia 76ers on opening night , falling to the Boston Celtics on Friday and dropping a 111-102 home game to an Orlando Magic team missing injured All-Star forward Paolo Banchero on Sunday — a game they led by 10 with 9:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, before conceding a 30-9 run over the next eight-plus minutes — the Knicks sit at 0-3 on the young season, one of only seven winless teams in the Association. New York suffered just four losing streaks of three or more games all of last season . Less than a week into its title defense, that counter already sits at one.

The Knicks are just the third defending champion in NBA history to begin the ensuing season with three consecutive losses, joining the 1969-70 Celtics and 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks. Those Mavericks won their fourth game , eventually finished as the West's No. 7 seed, and bowed out in the first round to the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Celtics, however, lost their fourth game , spent the entire season under .500 , and missed the playoffs for the first time in 20 years .

What's past isn't necessarily prologue; the Knicks aren't destined to follow in either the Mavs' or C's footsteps. Still, though: Kind of puts a little extra mustard on the outcome of New York's Tuesday night tilt with the Detroit Pistons, doesn't it?

Those Pistons — who finished with the No. 1 seed in the East last season, and who swept the Knicks by an average of 28 points per game during the regular season — improved to 3-0 on Sunday with a 106-93 road win over the Sixers. They figure to be champing at the bit for a shot at the champs … and, even without injured All-NBA center Jalen Duren , eminently capable of knocking the Knicks' lights out if New York can't find the 48 minutes' worth of tighten-the-screws attention to detail, crispness and physicality that Brown acknowledges has thus far eluded his club.

"It's the focus on the details," Brown told reporters after Sunday's loss. "You know, you go on a run, and then you come down and you throw the ball away. Like, probably three-fourths of our turnovers weren't from [the Magic's] pressure — and again, that's nothing against them, they beat us, I give them a lot of credit — but we throw the ball [low], we throw the ball and it goes through our hands, we jump in the air … and those turnovers, they convert the other way."

After averaging 13.6 turnovers per game during the 2025-26 regular season, and 13.5 cough-ups a contest in the playoffs , New York has given it up 16.3 times a night thus far . That increase in turnovers is the primary reason why the Knicks' margin in the possession battle has dropped from +2.9 possessions per game last season, according to Jared Dubin's analysis at Last Night in Basketball , to +1.9 through three games — still good, but not elite.

Combine that with Knicks opponents averaging 20.7 points per game off those turnovers — more than four points per game more than last season — and the margins that New York often mastered last season en route to 53 wins, a top-six point differential and eventually a title have grown considerably thinner.

"We do a pretty good job on some of the closeouts, and then other closeouts, we stop short, especially to a hot guy, and we let him shoot a comfortable shot," Brown said. "We play great defense, make them take a tough shot, and then we don't box out. Those are the little things that we've got to continue to embrace — especially when we're not shooting the ball well."

The Knicks are most certainly not shooting the ball well right now.

Their offensive process, by and large, hasn't been bad. The Knicks are generating a higher share of their shots at the rim this year than last while also taking an above-league-average percentage of their attempts from 3-point range — including the NBA's highest rate of corner 3s, which have accounted for 14% of New York's total field-goal attempts through three games, according to Cleaning the Glass .

Which is to say: The Knicks have broadly been creating a lot of the right kinds of looks, ranking in the top 10 in multiple shot quality and expected field-goal percentage metrics. The issue is, they're just not making many of them.

Through three games, the Knicks are shooting about 3% worse at the rim, 5% worse from 3-point land, and 16% worse on midrange tries than they did last season . Only one Knick, Karl-Anthony Towns, has made more than half of his shots; the other four members of New York's vaunted starting five have all been slow to get their shots online coming out of the gate.

Jalen Brunson, who spent much of his summer rehabilitating after undergoing surgery on his shooting wrist , sits under 40% from the field. OG Anunoby and Josh Hart are just barely above that mark. Mikal Bridges, whose mid-postseason turnaround was so vital to the Knicks' torrid run through the East during the springtime, has been positively frigid out of the gates: 5-for-23 from the field and 0-for-10 from 3-point range, for just 10 points in 90 minutes across three games.

All told, only the Chicago Bulls, Miami Heat and Toronto Raptors are underperforming their expected shot quality by more than the Knicks thus far, according to Synergy Sports Technology. That frozen start goes a long way toward explaining how a Knicks team that has ranked in the top seven in offensive efficiency in each of the last four seasons currently sits a dismal 29th in points scored per possession, and dead stinkin' last in half-court scoring efficiency .

Brunson spoke Sunday about the Knicks' need to tighten up their organization in the half-court — getting to the right spots, at the right pace, to execute properly and create the openings that can lead to cleaner looks and better scoring chances — which, ultimately, rests with their superstar point guard.

"Everything falls on my shoulders," said Brunson, who scored a team-high 28 points on 28 shot attempts against Orlando, in the Knicks' locker room after the loss. "I've just got to be a better leader when it comes to that, when it comes to making sure our guys are ready to go and in the right spots. There's a lot of other little things, but that's the main thing. It's just organization on my part."

That lack of organization and precision has been particularly notable in close-and-late situations, in which the Knicks — and Brunson, in particular — performed so brilliantly last season. New York has been outscored by a league-high 18 points in 10 minutes of "clutch" time thus far this season, according to NBA Advanced Stats , scoring well under one point per possession with more turnovers (four) than assists (two).

Brunson has missed five of his seven shots in those high-leverage moments — emblematic of the run of play for a Knicks squad that has thus far only intermittently resembled the team that locked into such an incredible offensive rhythm last postseason.

"We're not going to be the same," Brunson said. "We're not going to be the way we were playing last year. That's just human nature. But we have to accept this part of the journey, find a way to be better, and hopefully throughout a couple of games, we'll be able to look back and say, 'Hey, we grew from that.'"

The schedule does afford some get-right opportunities. After Tuesday's matchup with the undefeated Pistons, New York will play four of its next six games against the Chicago Bulls, Brooklyn Nets and Milwaukee Bucks — teams with a combined 1-8 record. Thaw out those jumpers a bit and get some regression to the mean in the overall shot-making, and New York could relocate its rhythm in a flash.

On the other hand, though, the Knicks feel a long way from prematurely marking those down as wins given the way they're misfiring right now.

"Games like [Sunday's loss to the Magic] will tell us that, you know, like I said before, our crap stinks," Brown said. "It does. And we're the only ones that can do something about it. There's no light switch that we can just turn on and think that we're going to go win ballgames. Nobody's going to give us anything."

No, the Knicks will have to take the wins they need to right the ship — and, as Brunson stressed, they'll have to do it by sticking together.

"One thing I said throughout the entire training camp, and honestly to this day, is: we're going to see who we are within the first couple of weeks of the season," Brunson said Sunday. "We're hitting adversity now. How are we going to respond?"

They need a collective response. Better shooting across the board. Better physicality at the point of attack from Bridges and Anunoby. Better foul avoidance from Towns, who's averaging a career-high 4.6 personals per 36 minutes. Better play in the middle when Towns hits the bench, with Andre Drummond coming back down to Earth after his strong first half in the season opener against Philly and James Wiseman providing up-and-down minutes on Sunday against Orlando.

Better everything, really. Except, maybe, better treatment from the adoring masses who spent the summer throwing flowers at the Knicks' feet.

"Everyone's been telling us what a great job we did — how fun it was, what we did for the city, the constant praise," Brunson said. "We need kind of, just … the opposite."

Well, Cap, I've got good news and bad news, and they're both the same thing. Keep playing like this, and the honeymoon period of that constant praise might be over a hell of a lot sooner than anybody anticipated.

articles.title: Reproche en el Real Madrid a los críticos: "Nadie se atreve a decírmelo a la cara"
articles.standfirst: Nick Smith Jr., en pleno proceso de adaptación al baloncesto europeo tras salir de la NBA, deja claro que "no tengo ninguna presión"
articles.summary: Nick Smith Jr., en pleno proceso de adaptación al baloncesto europeo tras salir de la NBA, deja claro que "no tengo ninguna presión"
articles.body: Nick Smith Jr., el joven anotador de 22 años con el que el Real Madrid cerró su plantilla, ha recurrido a X (Twitter) para contestar a algunos de sus críticos en redes sociales. "Métanse presión ustedes mismos. Por mi parte, no hay ninguna presión", apuntó el estadounidense, que está promediando 9,5 puntos (con un 60% de acierto en tiros de 2 puntos y un 17,6% en triples) en su primeros cuatro partidos en la Liga Endesa. El eléctrico escolta, que llegó a la ACB tras jugar en la NBA para Los Angeles Lakers y Charlotte Hornets, publicó que "muchos mensajes, pero ninguno de vosotros se atreve a decírmelo a la cara". "Estamos jugando como equipo y mejorando cada día; eso es lo único que importa. Mantengan esa misma energía", subrayó Nick Smith Jr., que fue el elegido por el Real Madrid tras valorar el equipo blanco la incorporación de Lester Quiñones, Lonnie Walker, Armoni Brooks o Ochai Agbaji.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown se revuelve contra 'La Mamba Blanca': "Es 10.000 % mentira"
articles.standfirst: Jaylen Brown desmiente de forma contudente la información de Brian Scalabrine de que exigiese el traspaso en los Boston Celtics
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown desmiente de forma contudente la información de Brian Scalabrine de que exigiese el traspaso en los Boston Celtics
articles.body: Jaylen Brown, alero de los Philadelphia 76ers de LeBron James, desmintió la información de Brian Scalabrine que sugiere exigió ser traspasado de los Boston Celtics. "Es 10.000 % mentira", le dejó claro Jaylen Brown a Kris Rhim de ESPN. El nuevo jugador de los Sixers llegó a Filadelfia en el traspaso de Paul George a los Celtics. Brian Scalabrine, exjugador NBA al que bautizaron de modo irónico como 'The White Mamba' (La Mamba Blanca) que actualmente es analista de NBC Sports Boston, aseguró que Jaylen Brown había solicitado salir de Boston, que presentó una serie de exigencias a los Celtics y que "deseaba ser traspasado a Milwaukee". Poco después el ex de Nets, Celtics y Bulls matizó sus comentarios, señalando que Brown "técnicamente no exigió ser traspasado", aunque reiteró que el jugador sí presentó una lista de exigencias a los Celtics. "No sé cuál fue el ultimátum, ni cuáles eran las exigencias o lo que fuera. Así que, técnicamente, no pidió ser traspasado. Fue algo así como: "Haced esto, o si no...". Y una de esas cosas podría haber sido: "Dadme la extensión de contrato de 140 millones de dólares... No he llegado al fondo de todo eso. Ni siquiera sabía que esto iba a convertirse en un tema. Es una de esas cosas que he tenido en mente durante meses. Al final lo mencioné porque estábamos hablando de cuestiones de lo más extrañas, y ahora ya ha salido a la luz", comentó Scalabrine.

articles.title: Bayern - Barça: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Los azulgranas afrontan una nueva cita europea a domicilio en Múnich
articles.summary: Los azulgranas afrontan una nueva cita europea a domicilio en Múnich
articles.body: La competición comienza a entrar en una fase en la que la acumulación de partidos obliga a mantener una enorme regularidad. Barça y Bayern ya han vivido todo tipo de situaciones durante las primeras semanas del torneo continental. El conjunto azulgrana abrió su participación con un triunfo por 89-82 contra Anadolu Efes, pero cayó después por 94-87 ante Dubai Basketball. Posteriormente se impuso por 95-82 a Besiktas, perdió en casa por 81-88 contra Zalgiris y volvió a ganar en la quinta jornada al derrotar por 90-87 al Maccabi. Bayern, por su parte, comenzó con una victoria por 84-86 sobre Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv, cayó 100-76 ante Fenerbahce, perdió 84-86 contra Partizan y 87-94 ante Virtus Bologna antes de imponerse por 93-101 a Anadolu Efes. Dos trayectorias con altibajos que convierten el encuentro de Múnich en una nueva oportunidad para ganar terreno en una competición extremadamente exigente. El Bayern Múnich-Barça se juega hoy martes 27 de octubre a las 20:00 horas, horario peninsular español. El partido entre Bayern Múnich y FC Barcelona podrá verse en España a través de M+ Baloncesto. La información de la jornada, los resultados y todo lo que suceda en la Euroliga se podrá seguir también en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Carlos Jiménez, nuevo coordinador de formación de las selecciones masculinas
articles.standfirst: Tendrá responsabilidad directa sobre la U20, U19, U18 y U17
articles.summary: Tendrá responsabilidad directa sobre la U20, U19, U18 y U17
articles.body: Carlos Jiménez, actual Team Manager de la Selección Masculina Absoluta, aumenta su responsabilidad en la Federación Española de Baloncesto y se une al Área Deportiva para asumir el cargo de Coordinador de Formación de Selecciones Masculinas. Con esta nueva responsabilidad, de especial relevancia en el organigrama deportivo de la FEB, Carlos Jiménez se encargará de coordinar a nivel técnico todas las selecciones masculinas de formación. Además, tendrá la responsabilidad directa sobre las selecciones U17, U18, U19 y U20, las últimas categorías antes de la Selección Absoluta. En sus nuevas funciones, Carlos Jiménez trabajará mano a mano con David Soria, que continúa ejerciendo como Coordinador de Formación de las Selecciones Masculinas entre las categorías U12 a U15 y, dentro de la estructura deportiva de la FEB, asume la responsabilidad directa sobre la U16. Junto a su nueva labor de coordinación, Carlos Jiménez mantiene su rol de Team Manager de la Selección Absoluta Masculina y Embajador de la FEB, así como su vínculo con la Liga U como representante de la Federación en la competición.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic refuses to back down after Nuggets fans boo the team as Draymond Green sends Warriors fans a message
articles.summary: Two days after telling booing fans to stay away, the Denver Nuggets center, Nikola Jokic said it again following Monday’s 134-114 home loss to the Golden
articles.body: Two days after telling booing fans to stay away, the Denver Nuggets center, Nikola Jokic said it again following Monday’s 134-114 home loss to the Golden State Warriors. Denver is 1-2, the defense is giving up points in bunches, and the crowd fell quiet. It began after a wild overtime win on Saturday, when Denver erased a 23-point hole while parts of the crowd jeered. Draymond Green has since weighed in, aimed at Warriors fans. Jokic also named what is wrong with this team, and the list was long.Why did Nikola Jokic stand by his comments about Nuggets fans?Asked about the boos again after Monday’s loss, the 31-year-old center did not budge. “I’m sticking to what I said,” Jokic told reporters. He has played in front of 10 people and in front of 15,000, but never heard a home crowd turn on its team. “I’m not used to fans booing their own team,” he said.Pressed on whether European crowds only boo opponents, the Serbian star said he had never heard of it. “Probably they are, but I think they’re not the real fans.”The first comment came after Saturday’s 141-135 overtime win over New Orleans, when Denver erased a 23-point deficit. Jokic had 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, including eight points in overtime. He said the fans who booed “don’t need to come anymore.”Monday brought no boos, even with the Warriors up 24 in the fourth quarter. Silence filled the arena. Denver trailed only 60-56 at halftime before the game got away, and Jokic finished with 19 points, seven rebounds and 11 assists.What did Draymond Green tell Warriors fans?Green backed Jokic on his podcast. “I agree with Jokic on this,” the Warriors forward said, adding “He is dead serious.” His view is plain. Fans who boo in the first home game show up with a negative mindset. Green still called fans great and said the game does not move forward without them.Denver trailed New Orleans 73-57 at the half on Saturday, and Green still found it baffling to boo in a home opener. Golden State is 1-3 after Monday’s win, and its crowd has stayed behind the team so far.Jokic had a bigger worry than the stands. Asked what Denver must fix, he said “everything,” then pointed hardest at defense. “We cannot defend.” The Nuggets rank 26th with a 119.3 defensive rating. Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo sat out Monday. Diallo could return Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET in New Orleans.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pistons out to prove No. 1 seed was no fluke as they face champion Knicks
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons have beaten three of the East's contenders so far this season with a mix of balanced scoring and improved shooting.
articles.body:
For the past six months, the Detroit Pistons have heard it all about their playoff failure.

A wave of roster changes and blockbuster trades in the Eastern Conference has all but relegated J.B. Bickerstaff's crew to an afterthought in championship oddsmakers' minds. But have the pundits gotten it wrong, so far? Maybe, but based on Detroit's early vacation from the postseason, it wasn't a stretch to question their realistic title aspirations.

The team with the conference's best regular-season record in 2025-26 needed seven games to beat the Orlando Magic in the first round after falling behind 2-0, then was bounced in the semifinals by the Cleveland Cavaliers, losing by 31 at home in Game 7.

See the coolest sneakers of the NBA season

An offseason of reflection revealed two obvious things: averaging 117 points a game in the regular season means nothing without a competent outside shooter, and an extra ball handler would take the load off star Cade Cunningham, who doesn't have to facilitate the offense on every possession.

The drama didn't stop there, as Jalen Duren, who earned third-team All-NBA honors, was in a standoff with his contract before finally signing a five-year, $200 million extension before the season .

Detroit will have to do without the services of Duren for at least the next two weeks after he injured his hamstring, and forward Ausar Thompson, who led the league in steals and was an All-NBA First-Team All-Defensive pick, is nursing an ankle injury.

Despite that, the word fluke hasn't been used this season, as Detroit has dispatched three teams considered their closest competition in the East with victories over the Boston Celtics, Miami Heat and Philadelphia 76ers , the last two on the road, while also vastly improving their 3-point shooting so far.

Last season, the Pistons hit only 36% of their shots from downtown, and in the first three games, that percentage has jumped to 42%. That kind of deadly accuracy isn't sustainable over an 82-game season, but it will force teams to play the perimeter and respect any player who hovers around the 3-point line, especially when defending Duncan Robinson, who can fight off screens and bury long-range shots against uninterested, lazy defenders.

Cunningham, a first-team All-NBA selection, leads the team in scoring, assists, steals and blocks, all the while playing most possessions off the ball, but has been aided by the 32-year-old Robinson and John Collins, who signed a 3-year, $51 million deal in the offseason and brings another veteran presence who can hold down the fort should Thompson and Duren miss extended time. In the season's first three games, three different players have led the team in scoring.

"We're just staying steady. We're not getting ahead of ourselves," Cunningham said after the 76ers victory. "The togetherness is there. We got a great system, we got the best coach in the league."

The early three-game road trip ends at Madison Square Garden against the New York Knicks , who are still seeking their first victory and are looking to avoid becoming the first defending champion to start the season 0-4 since the Boston Celtics in 1969, their first season without legend Bill Russell.

Detroit beat the Knicks in all three meetings last season, and it will be interesting to see if the Pistons can maintain their shooting touch and defensive intensity against a desperate New York squad that is back as an Eastern Conference favorite.

articles.title: Auburn basketball fires GM Brian Kloman. What went wrong with Mantas Rubstavicius?
articles.summary: Auburn basketball fired GM Brian Kloman after an eligibility issue involving Mantas Rubstavicius, who will not play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body:
Auburn basketball has fired general manager Brian Kloman following information that showed Kloman failed to disclose eligibility requirements regarding international signee Mantas Rubstavicius, the Montgomery Advertiser, part of the USA TODAY Network, reported Monday, Oct. 26.

Rubstavicius also voluntarily ended his eligibility lawsuit, meaning he won't play for Auburn this season. Both changes regarding Kloman and Rubstavicius were confirmed by Auburn , per the report.

Kloman was aware of Rubstavicius having previously enrolled in college classes overseas, but didn't tell Auburn or Rubstavicius' representation, per the report. Rubstavicius declined to sign an affidavit that stated he had never enrolled in college, which led to him dismissing his lawsuit.

Kloman was fired just seven months into his tenure.

"Rather than continue with the uncertainty associated with my ongoing lawsuit, I have decided to pursue an opportunity in Europe," Rubstavicius said in a statement. "I want to thank the Auburn administration, Coach [Steven] Pearl, and my teammates for all their support during my time here. I wish them all success."

Rubstavicius, a 6-6 guard from Lithuania, never competed in college, nor signed an NBA or G League contract, although he played in 2024 Summer League for the Golden State Warriors. The 24-year-old played professionally for Zalgiris Kaunas of the Lithuanian Basketball League before signing with the Tigers.

Rubstavicius' final appeal regarding his eligibility was denied in October. According to court documents cited in the report, he had also already signed "binding" revenue-sharing contracts and financial aid agreements with Auburn.

Kloman, a longtime staffer of Louisville coach Pat Kelsey, was with Kelsey for 11 years across stops at Winthrop, College of Charleston and Louisville.

"Mantas is an exceptional young man with a bright future ahead of him," Pearl said in a statement. "We appreciate the time he spent as part of our Auburn basketball family and wish him nothing but success as he takes this next step in his career. We look forward to following his success both on and off the court."

articles.title: A Blockbuster Trade Idea to Fix Miami's Growing Bam Problem
articles.summary: The Miami Heat and New York Knicks entered the 2026-27 season with high expectations. Miami won the protracted Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes, trading for the former NBA MVP from the Milwaukee Bucks in July.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat and New York Knicks entered the 2026-27 season with high expectations. Miami won the protracted Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes, trading for the former NBA MVP from the Milwaukee Bucks in July.

The Knicks won their first championship in 53 years, but they haven't defended the title well. Outside of swapping in Andre Drummond for Mitchell Robinson, New York has the same core roster.

Maybe the hangover wears off, but neither team has won in a combined seven games. If the slow starts continue, they could help each other with an early two-team deal.

The Miami Heat receive: Karl-Anthony Towns, $6.1 million trade exception (Tim Hardaway Jr.)

The New York Knicks receive: Bam Adebayo, Tim Hardaway Jr.

In April, Heat president Pat Riley suggested the team's asking price in trade for Adebayo was eight picks and San Antonio Spurs All-Star Victor Wembanyama.

That was before the franchise went all-in on Antetokounmpo, losing significant shooting and playmaking in the process. Adebayo and Antetokounmpo could be a devastating defensive pairing, but if Miami's offense can't score, the 2026-27 campaign may be long and painful.

Towns, now an NBA champion, is nowhere near Adebayo's defensive capability. While the Heat's center stunned the world with an 83-point game last year, he's nowhere near Towns as a scorer or shooter. Adebayo averages 16.2 points per game and shoots 31.4 percent from three. Towns' 22.7 points and 39.8 percent shooting immediately change Miami's offensive spacing.

The team is close to its $209 million first-apron hard cap, so it will need to include Hardaway, who hasn't shot well, after his December 15 trade restriction lifts. An immediate fix to staunch the bleeding would require one of Andrew Wiggins, Bobby Portis, or Davion Mitchell instead, along with a third team to ease the Knicks' apron issues.

Miami still needs playmaking support, but the cultural shift from Adebayo to Antetokounmpo started the moment the Heat agreed to the deal with the Bucks. Towns has a $61 million player option for 2027-28, but he'll opt out if offered an extension he deems viable. At this point, he and the Knicks have reached an impasse, reportedly stopping at a $200 million offer over four additional seasons, per Stefan Bondy of the New York Post.

After a trade, the Heat can pay a similar annual rate of $150 million over three years—starting at about $47.6 million, almost $6 million below Adebayo's salary next season.

The fans won't like the Knicks' motivation for the deal: money.

The championship vibes were disrupted this offseason when Towns and the team couldn't agree to a contract extension. Towns, almost 31, was willing to opt out of his $61 million player option to lock in a new deal starting near $50 million for 2027-28.

The Knicks tabled discussions, leaving Towns frustrated. Similarly, starter Josh Hart will need to wait for his next deal. Don't point the finger at the pair for torching chemistry; the roster expects to be rewarded for delivering a title. When the organization doesn't come through, it doesn't go unnoticed.

Then there was the championship ring " mistake ": assistant coaches and employees were left out of the celebration and instead received a phishing email in a network security test. The issues aren't stemming from the players.

Putting aside the drama, Adebayo, 29, has a fixed cost of $53.4 million for 2027-28, followed by a player option at $57.4 million. The team has time before it has to recommit to Adebayo, who is significantly better than Towns defensively.

While Adebayo isn't a reliable three-point shooter, don't forget he scored 83 points last season. He'd eventually become a fan favorite once the city gets over losing Towns, a core piece of the title team.

Hardaway spent the early part of his career in New York and will undoubtedly regain his shooting stroke alongside a playmaker like Jalen Brunson. The Knicks are very close to their $221.7 million second-apron hard cap, but Adebayo and Hardaway combined earn less this season than Towns.

It would be bold to move on from Towns so quickly, but it's also bold not to extend him after his championship-caliber performance.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Timeline to Return to Raptors amid Knee Swelling
articles.summary: Having already missed one game due to a knee injury, the Toronto Raptors are preparing to be without Kawhi Leonard for an extended period.
articles.body:
Having already missed one game due to a knee injury, the Toronto Raptors are preparing to be without Kawhi Leonard for an extended period.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania , Leonard is expected to miss "a period of weeks" due to swelling in his left knee after an MRI revealed no structural damage.

The Raptors said in a statement that Leonard will be reevaluated in one week.

Leonard has not historically had major injury issues in his left knee. His right knee had the torn ACL during the 2021 playoffs and torn meniscus during the 2023 playoffs.

The Raptors held Leonard out of Sunday's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves due to swelling in the knee. His absence came after playing under 30 minutes in each of Toronto's first two games.

Leonard had a slow ramp-up to the start of the regular season. He sat out he first two preseason games before making his debut on Oct. 13 against the New York Knicks.

In the two preseason contests Leonard played, he was on the floor for a total of 40 minutes. He played well in his first game with 21 points in 17 minutes.

Following the Raptors' 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves, head coach Darko Rajaković told reporters Leonard was set to undergo further testing after noticing an issue with his knee during his pregame warmup routine.

Leonard's performance in his first two regular-season games wasn't up to his usual standard. The seven-time All-Star shot 32.4 percent from the field, though he added 15 rebounds and seven steals in two Raptors wins.

The Raptors acquired Leonard in an offseason trade with the Los Angeles Clippers to bring him back to Toronto for the first time since leading the franchise to an NBA title during the 2018-19 season.

Leonard signed a two-year, $115 million contract extension in September that ties him to the Raptors through at least the 2027-28 season. He has a $58.9 million player option for 2028-29.

Third-year guard Ja'Kobe Walter took Leonard's spot in the starting lineup against Minnesota.

The Raptors still have enough top-end talent with Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett to win while Leonard is out, but their ceiling in the Eastern Conference depends on how many games the two-time NBA Finals MVP is able to play this season.

Toronto will be back in action on Wednesday when it hosts the Orlando Magic at Scotiabank Arena.

articles.title: Allen Iverson Makes Bold Prediction About LeBron's 1st Season With 76ers, 'I Know for a Fact'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers legend Allen Iverson is supremely confident in what the team will achieve after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers legend Allen Iverson is supremely confident in what the team will achieve after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

"I know. I know for a fact it's going to happen," he said while guaranteeing an NBA Finals win, per Jeff Skversky of Fox 29 Philadelphia. "It's gonna end with a parade. I promise you that."

The Sixers are off to a 3-1 start, which includes wins over the New York Knicks and Cleveland Cavaliers. James is settling into a secondary role, while Brown is thriving as a shooter (42.1 percent on threes).

Elsewhere, two notable championship contenders are showing some cracks. The 0-3 Knicks don't have the same sharpness they showed in the 2026 playoffs, while the Oklahoma City Thunder will be without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for most or all of the season.

Philadelphia's lack of center depth behind Joel Embiid is something to monitor, though. James doesn't sound enthusiastic about playing the 5 on a regular basis, and the jury is out on Adem Bona as the backup big.

In general, the bench doesn't inspire a ton of confidence. With Embiid and VJ Edgecombe unavailable, only eight players saw on the floor in a 106-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons.

Would you consider the Sixers to be the clear Finals favorites? Maybe not.

But you can't blame Iverson for feeling this confident after the opening week.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Let's put the blame for the Game 6 scheduling debacle where it belongs — with the league and the Dream
articles.summary: When we assign the well-deserved blame for this Game 6 embarrassment, let's at least get it right.
articles.body:
There is a chance the WNBA season will end in the middle of the afternoon in Atlanta on Thursday, with the Golden State Valkyries being rushed off the floor at State Farm Arena to celebrate in a practice gym so that workers have enough time to get the venue ready for an NBA game later that night.

For a league that has broken through into the mainstream and proven the product can unapologetically stand on its own in terms of TV ratings and sold-out buildings, it's pretty much a disaster scenario. For many WNBA fans who endured years of disrespect, only to see the league's social currency explode over the last few years, starting a potential Finals-clinching game at 12:30 p.m. ET on a weekday no doubt feels like a return to second-class citizenry.

But fans who are crying foul over how the WNBA and the Atlanta Dream decided Monday to navigate an impossible scheduling conflict also need to understand this: The WNBA has long since become a viable basketball business that should be talked about as such, not a social and moral cause that needs the NBA to come clean up its mess.

So when we assign the well-deserved blame for this Game 6 embarrassment, let's at least get it right.

It's not happening because of misogyny. Or because the NBA is failing to support a league of which it owns 42%. Or because the Atlanta Hawks are being inflexible with their schedule or the arena whose dates they control.

It's happening because the WNBA and the Atlanta Dream messed up, waited until the last minute for a fix and settled for what they believed the best of several bad options.

They might not be right about that, by the way. If the only viable choices were to play Game 6 in the early afternoon so the arena could be turned around in time for the Atlanta Hawks-Cleveland Cavaliers game that night or to play in prime time in the Dream's madhouse of a 3,500-seat arena where they normally play, the WNBA as a whole would probably be better served by the more favorable TV window. Fans of the Valkyries, who lead the series 3-2, will have to watch basketball with a side of morning coffee.

No wonder so many fans are celebrating the imminent departure of commissioner Cathy Engelbert, whose legacy will be leaving behind a league both transformed by once-unthinkable popularity and overrun with very predictable nonsense.

We can debate how many of the WNBA's endless narrative peccadillos are actually its fault — hardly anyone can outrun the Internet outrage machine these days — but it would help immensely if the league's most hardcore supporters knew the proper place to direct their outrage when things don't go as planned.

And in this case, the NBA and the Atlanta Hawks do not deserve the shrapnel.

Yes, it would be better for everyone if Game 6 took place in prime time, in a sold-out State Farm Arena. Yes, a WNBA Finals game is more "important" in a global sense than a regular-season NBA game in late October.

But when you see people like women's basketball great Rebecca Lobo suggest on social media that it would be "positive PR for the Hawks" if they agreed to swap arenas on Thursday night, it comes across more like pie-in-the-sky WNBA activism than anything resembling a serious idea.

The Hawks, by the way, did agree to move their tip-off time back by an hour, from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m., to make this happen. They did the same last Saturday to accommodate Game 4 because State Farm Arena hasn't actually been available on any of the dates the WNBA had originally pegged for Games 3, 4 and 6.

But other solutions were non-starters. The Hawks and Cavs both play on Wednesday, so there was no way they could play Thursday afternoon, particularly with Cleveland having to travel.

Others suggested the Hawks and Cavs swap home games and play in Atlanta later in the season, but that comes with complications, too, when you're talking about 72 hours notice. Moving the game to Friday would have created a back-to-back with travel for the Hawks, putting them at a competitive disadvantage. It turns out you can't just move the NBA schedule around like a dinner reservation.

And suggesting the Hawks should willingly play in a 3,500-seat arena, losing millions of dollars and ticking off roughly 14,000 people who had planned to be there Thursday night to accommodate a team they don't even have common ownership with? It's laughable. The Hawks have more than twice as many season ticket-holders than could fit into that place. How would you even decide who got seats?

This isn't even about a value judgment between the WNBA Finals and an NBA regular-season game. Anyone with genuine interest in the WNBA as a product and not just a social media engagement tool would agree that the league deserves better than what it's getting Thursday night.

It's simply a logistics issue, and it's the WNBA's responsibility to deliver solutions.

In this case, the root issue is that the Atlanta Dream signed up coming out of COVID to make Gateway Center, a small multipurpose building near the Atlanta airport, their primary arena. With a better team, the WNBA's popularity explosion and the acquisition of superstar Angel Reese, they have now outgrown it, moving some of their marquee games and playoff games to State Farm. Next season, they'll share the building full time with the Hawks so this shouldn't be an issue.

But this year, potential Finals dates weren't blocked out for State Farm, which became even more of a problem because the WNBA season took a midseason break for the FIBA Women's World Cup and extended into the NBA regular season (the 2025 Finals ended on Oct. 10).

So because the Dream aren't owned by the Hawks and aren't permanent tenants of the arena, it was up to the team and the WNBA to work around the State Farm schedule, not the other way around. And this is the result: a potential final game of perhaps the league's best-ever season decided on a weekday afternoon with fewer people watching on TV and a potential rushed celebration with arena workers waiting to dismantle the floor.

It's not the end of the world, but it's a bad look and a problem that didn't have to consume so much of the oxygen from this series.

We also need to be clear-eyed about why it happened, who's at fault and that the range of solutions was limited.

The WNBA has broken into the big time, but a Finals game on a Thursday afternoon will inevitably look small. Trying to turn this into an NBA-vs.-WNBA issue will make everyone involved look only smaller.

articles.title: Matt Painter Gets Raise on Purdue Contract, Full Details Revealed Ahead of 2026-27 CBB Season
articles.summary: Purdue head coach Matt Painter's contract was updated heading into the 2026-27 college basketball season.
articles.body:
Purdue head coach Matt Painter's contract was updated heading into the 2026-27 college basketball season.

According to ESPN's Pete Thamel , Painter and the school agreed to an amended contract that includes a salary raise from $5.2 million to $7 million for the upcoming season. He'll now be among the 10 highest-paid coaches in the sport.

The deal also escalates by $50,000 each year, per Thamel.

Painter is under contract through the 2030-31 season following the agreement, per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN ).

He's entering his 22nd year as head coach of the Boilermakers.

"Purdue is a very special place for me, and it's an honor to continue to be the head basketball coach at my alma mater," Painter said regarding the amended contract, per the school's official website . "I'm humbled that the Purdue administration continues to put their faith in me to lead this program, and am excited to continue to elevate our program with class and strive to reach all of our goals on and off the court."

Painter owns a 501-224 record throughout his tenure at Purdue, sitting at No. 2 on the school's all-time coaching wins list .

He's helped the Boilermakers advance to the NCAA Tournament in 17 separate seasons, including a current streak of 11 consecutive March Madness appearances. Purdue also earned a spot in the national championship game in 2024.

Painter has won five Big Ten Coach of the Year awards while helping his team capture five Big Ten regular-season titles and three conference tournament championships.

For the 2026-27 season, the Boilermakers are looking to remain competitive in the Big Ten following the departures of seniors Braden Smith, Fletcher Loyer, and Trey Kaufman-Renn.

Purdue will open the regular season against No. 15 Gonzaga on Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo Says He's Been Labeled 'Scapegoat' by 'Outside' Critics amid Heat's 0-4 Start
articles.summary: Bam Adebayo discussed the criticism that he's received while the Miami Heat have opened the 2026-27 season with four straight losses.
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo discussed the criticism that he's received while the Miami Heat have opened the 2026-27 season with four straight losses.

"You know, it's funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat," Adebayo said, per ESPN . "But when the tables turn, just all that energy -- when the energy shifts -- just be prepared for that."

The three-time All-Star is averaging 11.8 points and 7.3 rebounds per game while shooting just 40.0 percent from the field and 16.7 percent from three-point range.

Adebayo has remained impactful defensively by recording 2.0 steals and 0.8 blocks on a nightly basis, but Miami is still winless despite the offseason addition of two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"I got expectations for myself, but, obviously, the outside noise got expectations for us," Adebayo said, per ESPN. "So for me, I know what I'm capable of. I'm not going to overthink that. We're 0-4 right now. I'd rather it be right now than this be midway through the season or in April. Because what if we go on a 10-game winning streak? Then how does the noise change?"

While the 29-year-old is largely known for his defensive acumen, he made strides on offense during his 2025-26 campaign.

Last season, Adebayo's average of 20.1 points per game represented the second-highest mark of his career. He also connected on a personal-best 127 three-pointers, leading to the hope that he could help space the floor for Antetokounmpo.

It hasn't worked out so far, as Miami ranks 27thamong all teams with a 105.3 offensive rating to open the year (via NBA.com ).

The Heat's offensive woes have been exacerbated when their two stars share the court.

Miami owns a minus-31.6 net rating in the 71 minutes that Adebayo and Antetokounmpo have played together (via NBA.com ).

The Heat will attempt to pick up their first win of the season during a matchup with the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday. Tip-off is at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Muggsy Bogues to Have Jersey Retired by Hornets, Holds Record as Shortest Player in NBA History
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets are set to honor one of the most beloved players in franchise history later this year.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets are set to honor one of the most beloved players in franchise history later this year.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday that on Feb. 11, the Hornets will retire the No. 1 jersey for former point guard Muggsy Bogues, who holds the record as the shortest player in NBA history at 5'3" and remains Charlotte's franchise leader in assists, steals and minutes.

The Hornets' decision to retire Bogues' jersey comes after their offseason trade that sent star point guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Ball had worn the No. 1 jersey since being selected with the third overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft.

The walking embodiment of "heart over height," Bogues spent 10 of his 14 NBA seasons in Charlotte. The Hornets selected him in the 1988 expansion draft, and he helped lead the team from mediocrity to playoff contention. After four straight seasons with fewer than 40 wins, Bogues helped lead Charlotte to three postseason appearances over the next five years, with two 50-win seasons in that span.

When Bogues was traded away in 1997, he was one of two players remaining from the original 1988 Hornets team, along with Dell Curry. He will now join Curry (No. 30) and Bobby Phills (No. 13) as the only players to have their jerseys retired in Charlotte.

Bogues helped pave the way for small guards to excel in the NBA. Players like Hall of Famer Allen Iverson and Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry followed in his footsteps and overcame their height limitations to achieve success.

This year's Hornets team has started the season with a 3-1 record, fueling optimism that it can emerge as a playoff contender. Bogues' upcoming jersey retirment will add to the positive vibes in Charlotte as the franchise turns the corner in its rebuild.

articles.body: Paul Pierce is facing a financial challenge away from the basketball court. He reportedly has around $300,000 in bank accounts while dealing with tens of thousands of dollars in monthly expenses.Paul Pierce claims his Fox Sports income has dried upAccording to court documents obtained by TMZ, Pierce's attorney described him as “drowning financially” and said he would have great difficulty paying additional legal costs requested by his ex, Princess Santiago. These figures reflect the financial position he described in the court documents, rather than a complete assessment of his wealth.$48,000 in monthly bills adds to the pressureThe figures listed in the filing show how much Pierce says he spends each month. Apart from his support payments, he reportedly has around $48,000 in regular monthly bills.These include approximately $8,000 for childcare, $5,000 for groceries, $7,000 for dining out, $3,200 for utilities, $1,000 for clothing and $3,500 for entertainment, along with other expenses.Pierce also says he pays around $28,000 in child support and $20,000 in spousal support each month. articles.title: Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen Injury Updates, Latest News and Return Timelines for Jazz Stars
articles.summary: After having his 2025-26 season cut short by knee surgery, Utah Jazz center Jaren Jackson Jr. has suffered another setback.
articles.body:
After having his 2025-26 season cut short by knee surgery, Utah Jazz center Jaren Jackson Jr. has suffered another setback.

The Jazz announced that Jackson suffered a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for six to eight weeks. ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon reported that he will not require surgery. The team also announced that veteran forward Lauri Markkanen is considered day-to-day with a wrist injury.

Jackson exited Monday night's game against the Memphis Grizzlies with 10:04 remaining in the second quarter after injuring his right knee. He had six points, three rebounds and two assists in 10 minutes as the Jazz went on to suffer a 110-105 loss. Markkanen also left the game early after injuring his wrist in the first quarter.

Through Utah's first three games, Jackson averaged 19.7 points and 5.7 rebounds. He was also limited to three games with the Jazz last season after being acquired from the Grizzlies at the trade deadline due to his season-ending knee surgery.

Jackson was once regarded as one of the best two-way big men in the league, earning Defensive Player of the Year honors in 2023. However, he's developed a reputation for being injury-prone, appearing in 70 or more games just twice in his nine-year career.

Without Jackson in the lineup, Jaxson Hayes, Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba will be Utah's options at center. Hayes missed Monday's game with a shoulder injury, and Bamba filled in nicely with 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks.

The Jazz (1-3) will try to get used to life without Jackson when they face the San Antonio Spurs (1-2) on Wednesday.

articles.title: Jazz C Jaren Jackson Jr. has torn MCL, out at least 6 weeks; Lauri Markkanen day-to-day with wrist sprain
articles.summary: Jackson sustained his injury Monday in a game against his former Grizzlies.
articles.body:
Utah Jazz center Jaren Jackson Jr. has a torn MCL in his right knee and will miss at least six weeks.

The Jazz announced Jackson's diagnosis Tuesday after he sustained the injury Monday night in a 110-105 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies . Jackson isn't expected to undergo surgery.

Former All-Star Lauri Markkanen also left Monday's game with a wrist injury. The Jazz announced Tuesday that he has a sprained right wrist and is considered day-to-day.

A two-time All-Star and former Defensive Player of the Year, Jackson is a centerpiece of a revamped Jazz roster that hopes to compete for a playoff spot this season after four straight years of missing the postseason.

The Jazz acquired Jackson from the Grizzlies at last season's trade deadline, signaling their intent to return to competitiveness this season amid a 22-60 campaign that secured the No. 2 pick in the draft and the rights to select Darryn Peterson.

Jackson had surgery on his right knee shortly after joining the Jazz to remove a non-cancerous pigmented villonodular synovitis growth in his left knee. He played just three games in his first season with the Jazz and will now be sidelined for a significant portion of the season.

Jackson's injury occurred when Memphis guard Ty Jerome fell into his right leg after driving to the basket. Jackson's knee buckled, and he fell to the court in pain.

Jackson was able to stand and walk off the court with the help of teammates, but the Jazz ruled him out before the game was over.

The injuries to Jackson and Markkanen compound an already disappointing start to Utah's season. Tuesday's loss dropped the Jazz to 1-3. They're scheduled to face the reigning Western Conference champion Spurs in two of their next three games with a matchup against the 2-0 Trail Blazers in between. Markkanen's status for those games is unclear.

When healthy, the Jazz feature a promising core of Jackson, Markkanen, Peterson, standout point guard Keyonte George and Ace Bailey, the No. 5 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft. articles.title: WNBA's bizarre national anthem controversy shows just how much the league needs Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's absence from the WNBA Finals exposed how the national anthem controversy went unnoticed all season for the Dream and Valkyries.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark isn't quite the women's basketball equivalent of Tiger Woods, but there's a reason she's been compared to the 15-time major champion. She brought millions of new eyeballs to a league that had long struggled for mainstream attention. She's also a marketing juggernaut, with endorsement deals from the likes of Nike, Gatorade and State Farm. But like Tiger in his prime, perhaps the greatest measure of Clark's star power is that when she's absent — the audience is, too. Nothing illustrates that phenomenon better than the WNBA's national anthem controversy. WNBA SILENT AFTER FINALS TEAMS SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM DESPITE RULE REQUIRING PLAYERS TO STAND AND LINE UP All year long, players and coaches from the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have been running off the court before the Star-Spangled Banner is played. Then, just after "the home of the brave" is sung, they return to the floor. Neither team has publicly explained why it follows this routine, nor have they said what the players and coaches do during those 90-some-odd seconds. But the wildest part of all this is that, until these WNBA Finals — nobody seemed to notice. If an NFL or NBA team had engaged in a similar practice during the regular season, it would be one of the biggest sports stories — or even news stories — in the country. Pundits would be regularly weighing in on the matter, activists would be mobilizing, and a nationwide debate on the issue would ensue. WNBA FINALS: ANGEL REESE HEADLINES CHAMPIONSHIP SHOWDOWN AS LEAGUE SEEKS TO DRAW VIEWERS WITHOUT CAITLIN CLARK But until now, it had barely even generated a whisper. Do you think that would be the case if the Fever left the court for the anthem? The answer, of course, is "absolutely not." The actions of Clark and her teammates would be dissected every day. POTUS would probably comment, and some of those endorsement deals would be in jeopardy. But a Caitlin-free WNBA game simply doesn't matter to the majority of American sports fans. The scheduled start time for Game 6 speaks to that. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Monday, it was announced that what could be the final WNBA game of the season will be played at 12:30 p.m. Eastern time on a Thursday. The reasoning is that the Dream wanted a venue change — moving the game from Gateway Center Arena (capacity 3,500) to State Farm Arena (17,000). The problem is that the Hawks are scheduled to play that same day, meaning Game 6 will occur when most Americans are working or in school. Again, it's hard to believe that happens if Clark and the Fever were involved. This national anthem mystery is one of the more bizarre sports stories I've ever seen. That players and coaches have repeatedly left the court without offering an explanation is strange enough. That it's taken this long for anyone to notice might be even stranger. Without her, apparently, it's still remarkably easy.

articles.title: Ex-NBA guard Malik Beasley to plead guilty after involvement in gambling scheme
articles.summary: Malik Beasley was indicted in June after prosecutors said he manipulated several NBA games in a larger gambling scheme.
articles.body:
Longtime former NBA guard Malik Beasley has agreed to plead guilty to federal charges related to illegal sports gambling, his attorney told both The Athletic and ESPN on Tuesday.

Beasley, who was arrested earlier this summer, will officially enter his plea Dec. 9 in New York.

Beasley was indicted in June on federal charges related to a sports betting scheme alongside former NBA veteran Ed Davis. The duo, who played together for the Minnesota Timberwolves, were accused of working together to manipulate Beasley's performance in four games during the 2023-24 campaign. Beasley was on the Milwaukee Bucks at the time, and Davis was out of the league.

Beasley reportedly owed millions of dollars in a gambling debt, which led to Davis loaning Beasley money. But in order to pay off that debt, Beasley and Davis reportedly decided to launch a betting scheme. They allegedly worked with three others to place tens of thousands of dollars on a game that Beasley played in against the Cleveland Cavaliers that season. Beasley ended up scoring just three points in that game, well below his season average of 11.3 points per contest. Beasley is also accused of rigging a game against the Charlotte Hornets in similar fashion that same season.

Beasley has not played in the league since the 2024-25 season, which was one of the best in his career. He averaged 16.3 points per game, his best output in years, and finished second in the Sixth Man of the Year race while with the Detroit Pistons. He was due for a big payday after that season, too, but his free agency was interrupted both by a federal gambling investigation and an NBA investigation into Beasley. He went unsigned and hasn't played since.

Prosecutors alleged that Davis was in charge of the scheme. They were two of six men indicted in the scheme.

Beasley is the second active NBA player to plead guilty to charges related to gambling in the NBA. Jontay Porter was the first and pleaded guilty in July 2024 amid a separate but similar scheme. The NBA banned him for life in 2024 . It's unclear if Beasley will face that same fate.

articles.title: NBA Champion Paul Pierce Claims He’s ‘Drowning Financially’ in Filings Against Ex-Girlfriend
articles.summary: Pierce confirmed he is the father of Princess Santiago’s baby in March
articles.body:
NBA champion Paul Pierce says he is "drowning financially" in new court documents obtained by PEOPLE

Pierce was ordered to pay $100,000 in attorney's fees in addition to child support to his ex-girlfriend, Princess Santiago

After losing his job at Fox Sports, Pierce is "tapped out" financially, his attorney said

NBA champion Paul Pierce claims he is "drowning financially" as he and his ex-girlfriend Princess Santiago battle for custody.

According to documents obtained and reviewed by PEOPLE, a lawyer representing Pierce, 49, said the former Celtics star is "tapped out" and not receiving income since losing his job at Fox Sports last year.

Santiago and Pierce share one child: son King Rafael, born in February 2026. During an Aug. 11 court appearance, Pierce was ordered to pay $100,000 in attorney's fees, on a payment plan, and an additional $10,000 for a forensic accountant, according to the documents.

His attorney said the fees "no longer reflect [Pierce's] actual income" and claimed he's "unable to keep up with his obligation to pay his own counsel and forensic accountant, let alone pay additional funds to the other side in attorney's fees and forensic accounting fees."

Prior to losing his gig at Fox Sports, Pierce was bringing in $119,000 monthly, according to the filing, and received the final payment from the network in August. "Having lost his Fox Sports contract, while simultaneously facing these substantial financial obligations, Respondent is drowning financially," the filing said.

Pierce claims child support costs him roughly $28,000 a month, as well as approximately $20,000 in spousal support, per the documents.

A rep for Pierce didn't immediately respond to PEOPLE's request for comment.

According to Spotrac , Pierce earned approximately $195 million over his 19 seasons in the NBA. In addition to King, Pierce shares three kids with his ex-wife Julie Landrum: daughter Prianna and sons Prince and Adrian.

In March, Santiago filed to establish a parental relationship and requested genetic testing from Pierce to establish that he is the baby's father. She also requested sole legal and physical custody of King with visitation for Pierce, as well as $29,811 per month in child support.

She asked that Pierce obtain and pay for health insurance for King and one-half of all her pregnancy, birth and post-birth medical expenses.

After Pierce confirmed he is the father, Santiago told PEOPLE in a statement: "I believe in growth, accountability and healthy co-parenting. Paul has finally made an effort to see King and I appreciate that. At this time, I am focused on maintaining stability and consistent, healthy decision-making for our son while he continues building a positive father-son relationship moving forward."

articles.title: Jaren Jackson Jr. injured against former Grizzlies team, out six weeks
articles.summary: Utah Jazz big man Jaren Jackson Jr. was injured against his former Memphis Grizzlies team and will miss at least six weeks.
articles.body:
Utah Jazz big man Jaren Jackson Jr. will be re-evaluated in six weeks after suffering a torn MCL in his right knee against the Memphis Grizzlies, the team announced on Oct. 27.

Jackson was injured early in the second quarter on Oct. 26 after Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome drove to the basket, was fouled and fell into Jackson's right knee. Jackson attempted to play through the injury for a couple of possessions before asking to be removed from the game.

Jackson's injury came against the team that drafted him No. 4 overall in the 2018 NBA Draft. He s pent nearly eight seasons with the Grizzlies before being traded to the Jazz on Feb. 3 of last season.

In his time in Memphis, Jackson was a two-time All-Star and the 2022-23 NBA Defensive Player of the Year.

Jackson's injury came in the second meeting this season between the Grizzlies and Jazz. Memphis has won both matchups.

See our best photos from Memphis Grizzlies' season opener vs Utah Jazz

Injuries are creating depth issues in Utah's frontcourt. The team is already without projected starting center Jusuf Nurkic due to a right foot injury.

When Memphis traded Jackson , it acquired three future first-round picks. One of the assets is the most favorable first-round pick between the Utah Jazz, Cleveland Cavaliers and Minnesota Timberwolves in 2027. Utah currently has the worst record of those teams, meaning Memphis would get its pick.

The Grizzlies are off to a 4-0 start for the second time in franchise history and first time since 2014. They'll head to the Moda Center for a matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers on Oct. 29 (9 p.m., CT, DAZN-MEM).

articles.standfirst: El escolta azulgrana se impone en una gran segunda parte a una tremenda actuación de Miles Norris y Jokubaitis, ambos con pasado en Barcelona
articles.summary: El escolta azulgrana se impone en una gran segunda parte a una tremenda actuación de Miles Norris y Jokubaitis, ambos con pasado en Barcelona
articles.body: El Barcelona afrontaba su segunda salida consecutiva tras la victoria en Milán, y quería repetir en Múnich. Los de Sekulic aprovecharon la visita a uno de los equipos de la parte de abajo para seguir su escala en la clasificación. Con un Kevin Punter que volvió a ser decisivo, -23 puntos-, el conjunto azulgrana consiguió su quinta victoria de la temporada a través de una trabajada victoria que volvió a tener en Robinson, Martin o Nebo unos perfectos actores secundarios. El encuentro empezó con ritmo anotador y pocas faltas. El Barcelona enfrentaba a varios jugadores que tuvo en sus filas, y Miles Norris parecía motivado para destacar por encima del resto. Seis puntos seguidos con tres poderosos mates animaban a la afición alemana, pero un gran Tyrese Martin, con siete puntos, respondía en lo que parecía un mano a mano. El conjunto azulgrana puso la primera máxima (13-21) a falta de 1:53 que Bayern reduciría a cuatro al término del primer cuarto. Y el parcial para los locales seguiría. El Barcelona encajó un 13-2 en el que sólo anotó Punter en cuatro minutos y medio. Sin embargo, varias acciones positivas de Nebo, que firmó la jugada más espectacular en un alley-oop con Robinson, volvieron a reflotar a los culés. Un cuarto que tuvo muchos cambios de liderato en el marcador, en gran parte, por la tremenda actuación de Norris, que seguía anotando hasta los 14 puntos y llevaba a los suyos uno arriba a vestuarios (42-41). El alero que debutó la temporada pasada en Euroliga con el Barcelona seguiría castigando desde el triple tras la reanudación en el que ya es su mejor partido en la competición (17 puntos), pero no le servía para lanzar a su equipo en el marcador. Fue entonces cuando aparecieron los principales anotadores azulgranas. Primero Justin Robinson, con alguna penetración a canasta, y después Kevin Punter, con varios lanzamientos desde más allá del 6,75, encarrilaron el 19-23 del tercer cuarto que culminó Balcerowski con varias canastas debajo del aro para marcharse tres arriba a los últimos diez minutos. En el último cuarto aparecieron más soldados para acompañar a Punter. Juan Núñez, que tuvo sus minutos por unas molestias de Umoja Gibson, lo hizo con varias asistencias de mucha calidad. Justin Robinson también aportó, antes de que cometiera su quinta personal a falta de cuatro minutos. El drama en la posición de base se acentuaría con la lesión del propio Núñez. Algo que castigaría en el lado contrario de la pista el otro 'ex'; Jokubaitis se destapó en la segunda parte para acabar con 17 puntos e inquietar el triunfo azulgrana, que finalmente cerró con varios tiros libres para darle la segunda victoria consecutiva a domicilio y ponerse con un 5-3 que le hace escalar puestos en la clasificación. 84 - Bayern Múnich (17-25-19-23): Jokubaitis (17), Obst (14), Norris (17), Beauchamp (4), Voitgmann (0) -cinco inicial-, da Silva (2), Washington (5), Jessup (6), Lucic (0), Hollatz (3), Thiemann (6) y Wiley (10). 88 - Barcelona (21-20-23-24): Punter (23), Robinson (11), Martin (12), Nkamhoua (2), Nebo (2) -cinco inicial-, Gibson (7), Umude (2), Brizuela (1), Núñez (2), Evbuomwan (5), Balcerowski (9) y Minaya (2). articles.title: Damian Lillard Reflects on Playing With Giannis, Bucks After Blazers Reunion, 'It Wasn't My Home'
articles.summary: Damian Lillard discussed his two-year stint on the Milwaukee Bucks alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo before coming back to the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
Damian Lillard discussed his two-year stint on the Milwaukee Bucks alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo before coming back to the Portland Trail Blazers.

"Doing something outside of Portland, playing with a great player like Giannis, I think that was a luxury that I hadn't experienced, playing with somebody that's gonna show up, he's gonna compete," Lillard said in an interview with ESPN's Chiney Ogwumike . "So that was fun for me. I could just feel that it wasn't my home."

Lillard spent the first 11 seasons of his NBA career with the Trail Blazers, establishing himself as a franchise icon before he was traded to the Bucks as part of a blockbuster swap in Sept. 2023.

At the time, Milwaukee was just two years removed from capturing a championship and was expected to compete for another title after Lillard joined forces with a two-time MVP in Antetokounmpo.

The Bucks opened the 2023-24 season with a 30-13 record, but still decided to fire head coach Adrian Griffin before ultimately replacing him with Doc Rivers.

Milwaukee struggled under Rivers, but still advanced to the playoffs with a 49-33 record. The Bucks suffered a first-round exit after Antetokounmpo was unable to suit up in the postseason due to a calf injury , though.

The following year, Milwaukee clinched another playoff appearance by finishing at 48-34.

Still, the Bucks couldn't advance beyond the first round of the postseason after Lillard suffered a torn Achilles .

The nine-time All-Star was waived by Milwaukee during the ensuing offseason before returning to the Trail Blazers on a three-year, $42 million contract.

Lillard missed the 2025-26 season while recovering from his Achilles tear, but Portland's all-time leading scorer has been able to suit up this year.

He's scored 44 points and dished out eight assists across the first two appearances of his 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: El Valencia tumba al Fenerbahce en un triunfo de muchos quilates
articles.standfirst: Los de Albert igualaron en intensidad a Fenerbahçe y lograron detener la reacción turca a falta de dos minutos para el final.
articles.summary: Los de Albert igualaron en intensidad a Fenerbahçe y lograron detener la reacción turca a falta de dos minutos para el final.
articles.body: Victoria de muchos quilates, de prestigio. Valencia Basket logró doblegar al rocoso Fenerbahçe en un partido que tuvo controlado con suficiencia hasta el último cuarto. Los de Xavi Albert lograron igual la intensidad defensiva de los turcos, el mejor equipo de la Euroliga en esa faceta y supieron aguantar la reacción final de los de Jasikevicius para llevarse la victoria. Un triple de Brooks cuando peor pintaba la cosa, acabó con la resistencia visitante. Fenerbahçe llegó a ponerse por delante a falta de dos minutos y medio, pero el partido se quedó en un Roig Arena que vibró hasta el final El duelo de estilos anunciado en el Roig Arena tardó muy poco en ponerse en juego. Valencia sabía que tenía que correr y anotar y el parcial de 8-0 de inicio ponía en órbita el partido de forma evidente. Tanto, que Jasikevicius tuvo que parar la arrancada Taronja con un 12-4 en el marcador que le olía a chamusquina. Pese a un Shorts demasiado fallón, el equipo de Xavi Albert le dio a los turcos de su propia medicina. Defensa dura, sin respiro ni concesiones. Solo nueve puntos de los visitantes en un primer cuarto para olvidar que acabó con diez de diferencia para Valencia y muy buenas sensaciones. El segundo cuarto arrancó con un pequeño espejismo ofensivo de los turcos que anotaron cuatro puntos consecutivos. Pero se quedó en eso, en un amago, balas de fogueo. Valencia seguía en su partido. Igualar en intensidad defensiva y anotar, aunque en esta fase de partido con más dificultad. En ese escenario, Short le sacó la tercera falta personal al aclamado Braxton Key (la ovación del Roig Arena a uno de los héroes de la pasada campaña se hizo notar), dejando a los visitantes sin una de sus armas más mortíferas sobre la pista. Short apareció justo en el momento necesario para darle electricidad a la cosa y Valencia se fue a un 33-18 que obligó de nuevo al técnico lituano de Fenerbahçe a parar el partido buscando salir del pozo. Jasikevicius lo intentó todo, incluso una protesta más airada de lo normal, castigada con técnica, para buscar la reacción de los suyos, que no daban el paso al frente mientras Valencia hacía camino, sin alardes, pero con una defensa férrea. El partido se fue al descanso con 11 de ventaja para los locales y con Fenerbahçe en unos míseros 25 puntos. La segunda parte arrancó con el efecto Mirotic pidiendo paso. Varios aciertos del veterano pivot mantenían a raya a un Fenerbahçe al que le faltaba un toque de corneta para engancharse realmente al partido. Los turco cayeron en la trampa de intercambiar golpes y ahí Valencia Basket tiene pocos rivales en Europa. Taylor y Shorts aceptaron el reto de correr y los locales se fueron otra vez a los 15 puntos de diferencia con aparente normalidad (49-34) mediado el tercer cuarto. La tímida reacción de los turcos la cortaron de raíz los de Albert con un triple de Brooks en transición que puso en el marcador la máxima diferencia del encuentro (60-44) a falta de un minuto para el final del tercer cuarto. Pese a las diferencias, Fenerbahçe no se desconectaban del partido y su arranque del último cuarto prometía emociones hasta el final. Los turcos empezaron a anotar con más facilidad y rompieron rápido la barrera de los diez puntos de diferencia. Había partido. Shield y Baldwin encontraron la inspiración perdida y obligaron a Valencia a parar el partido a falta de cuatro minutos para el final con un inquietante 72-69, la menor diferencia desde el inicio del encuentro. Nunca los turcos habían estado tan cerca. El partido empezaba de cero y en ese escenario Fenerbahçe creció y Valencia Basket se fue deshaciendo. De hecho, a falta de dos minutos y medio, los turco tomaron ventaja en el marcador por vez primer en todo el partido (75-76). La cosa pintaba fea, pero un par de acciones de Short y Brooks dejaron la reacción turca en nada y el partido se quedó en casa. Gran victoria taronja.

articles.title: Maledon comanda el enésimo vendaval ofensivo del Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El base galo brilla en la dirección (18+4+6) ante un Kosner Baskonia que pagó su falta de pívots ante el enorme Tavares (10+12+3 tapones)
articles.summary: El base galo brilla en la dirección (18+4+6) ante un Kosner Baskonia que pagó su falta de pívots ante el enorme Tavares (10+12+3 tapones)
articles.body: El Kosner Baskonia sacó a relucir el carácter que lleva en su ADN para intentar menguar el huracán Real Madrid a su paso por el Buesa Arena, y aunque en algunos momentos del partido lo logró, no le bastó y terminó siendo devastado por el formidable arsenal ofensivo de los blancos (86-104), comandados por el mariscal francés Theo Maledon (18+4+6), en su mejor momento desde que viste la camiseta madridista. Luwawu-Cabarrot (14+3), Jantunen (13) y Tavares (10+12+3 tapones) llevaron la voz cantante en el noveno triunfo seguido del conjunto blanco. El gigante madridista dominó sin aparente esfuerzo en las inmediaciones de ambos aros aprovechando la falta de pívots que volvió a lastrar a un Baskonia, que defendiendo algo mejor vivió de las embestidas de Lawson (17+6), Simmons (17+5), Stewart (13), Baugh (10+8 asistencias) y de un joven Joksimovic (12+4) que tiene un futuro prometedor. Cuando el presidente baskonista Josean Querejeta aún rumiaba la pañolada y la pitada que le dedicó su afición por el despido de Galbiati, el Madrid ya había demarrado con Jantunen y Procida haciendo estragos (4-15, min 6). Luego se sumaron al carro blanco Luwawu-Cabarrot, Jones y Campazzo para aumentar más la renta (14-30). El Baskonia ni defendía ni atacaba (5/13 t2 y 1/5 triples). Los triples de Okeke y Maledon pusieron la máxima para el Madrid (19-36, min 13), pero se relajó y Simmons reactivó a los vitorianos con 10 puntos seguidos. Joksimovic y Faried le secundaron para cerrar un parcial de 12-2 que les metió en el partido (37-44, min 18). Lawson y Joksimovic, con sendos triples, acercaron más a los baskonistas (52-58). Pero Feliz y Maledon espabilaron a un Madrid que con un 2+1 de Luwawu-Cabarrot y triples de Abalde y Jones igualó su máxima (59-76). Lawson rompió el colapso local con cinco puntos, pero un enchufado Luwawu-Cabarrot, con dos triples mantuvo la cómoda ventaja madridista (69-83, min 30). Un triple de Santos acercó al Baskonia por ultima vez (74-82, min 32), porque entonces volvió a aparecer Maledon para adueñarse del partido anotando y asistiendo a sus compañeros para comandar un parcial de 5-14 (79-96, min 37), dejando visto para sentencia un triunfo que abrocharon Procida y Feliz con sus triples (86-104). 86 - Kosner Baskonia (19+27+23+15): Baugh (10), Joksimovic (12), Stewarrt (13), Frisch (2) y Faried (7) -cinco inicial-, Lawson (17), Simmons (17), Spagnolo (-) y Santos (8). 104 - Real Madrid (30+26+27+18): Maledon (19), Feliz (12), Procida (5), Jantunen (13) y Tavares (10) -cinco inicial-, Shulga (-), Okeke (5), Abalde (8), Jones (13), Campazzo (3), Pradilla (2) y Luwawu-Cabarrot (14).
