articles.title: Anthony Edwards to Undergo Surgery on Knee Injury, Latest Rumors on Wolves Star's Return Timeline
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star guard Anthony Edwards will miss "up to two months" after undergoing arthroscopic right knee surgery, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star guard Anthony Edwards will miss "up to two months" after undergoing arthroscopic right knee surgery, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday.

Edwards was previously listed as questionable due to right knee injury management ahead of a Wednesday night game against the Golden State Warriors.

The news comes the day after Wolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters he thought Edwards' injury was a "daily situation" that didn't warrant "any long term concern," per The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski .

Edwards dealt with issues in both knees last season, including a left knee hyperextension and bone bruise during the Wolves' playoff run last April.

He previously missed time after an MRI revealed inflammation in his right knee in March.

Edwards felt pain in that knee starting in March and lasting into the playoffs, according to Krawczynski .

He later said he had taken two months away from basketball this offseason to allow his knees to heal, per Krawczynski .

Edwards could be seen grabbing at his right knee during a game against the Toronto Raptors last Sunday. He still averaged 48.1 percent shooting across 33.8 minutes per night during the Wolves' 3-1 start to the season.

The Wolves star also paced the NBA with 12.5 field goals per game while averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and two steals.

Edwards most recently played more than 41 minutes and dropped 47 points in a Monday night overtime loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

A two-month recovery timeline would likely sideline Edwards for about 25 games and put him on track to return in late December.

Whether Jaden McDaniels and LaMelo Ball can step up their offensive contributions over that stretch will determine if the Wolves are still on track for another playoff run by the time Edwards potentially returns to the court this winter.

articles.title: Aldama, cerca de estrenarse esta temporada y de debutar con los Mavericks
articles.standfirst: Tras ser asignado para entrenar con el equipo de la G League, es duda para medirse este jueves a los Thunder de Aday Mara
articles.summary: Tras ser asignado para entrenar con el equipo de la G League, es duda para medirse este jueves a los Thunder de Aday Mara
articles.body: El regreso de Santi Aldama a la pistas está cada vez más cerca y podría darse esta misma semana. El pívot canario ha sido calificado como duda de cara al encuentro de la madrugada de este jueves ante los Thunder. Podría ser su estreno como jugador de los Mavericks después de haber pasados sus primeras cinco campañas en la NBA en Memphis. Aldama fue asignado a los Texas Legends, el equipo vinculado de la G League, para realizar algún entrenamiento como parte de su protocolo de regreso a la actividad. La idea era que sólo se ejercitara y sería convocado de nuevo por los Mavericks sin haber llegado a jugar. Su estreno del curso y con su nueva camiseta ya se divisa. El pívot español no juega un partido desde el 4 de febrero. Se lesionó con los Grizzlies y en marzo se sometió a una artroscopia en la rodilla derecha. La operación acabó con su quinta temporada en la NBA. También se ha perdido partidos de la selección española correspondientes a las Ventanas FIBA y el arranque de la temporada actual. Si el estreno de Aldama fuera este jueves ante los Thunder se las vería con Aday Mara en un duelo interior entre españoles. Sin embargo, quizás no pudiera coincidir con Sergio De Larrea. El base, su compañero en los Mavericks, tuvo que retirarse en el último partido después de lastimarse una rodilla. Está pendiente de nuevas pruebas para conocer el diagnóstico exacto y, aunque no parece grave, podría faltar a algún partido.

articles.title: Plaga de lesiones en el inicio de la NBA: Anthony Edwards, Kawhi, Jaren Jackson Jr...
articles.standfirst: Las tres estrellas se perderán un mínimo de varias semanas y se suman en la enfermería a Jalen Williams y Cason Wallace
articles.summary: Las tres estrellas se perderán un mínimo de varias semanas y se suman en la enfermería a Jalen Williams y Cason Wallace
articles.body: La NBA vive una plaga de lesiones en este comienzo de temporada. En un par de jornadas aciagas, la competición va acumulando importantes nombres en la enfermería. Los últimos en caer han sido Kawhi Leonard, Anthony Edwards y Jaren Jackson Jr. El alero, en su regreso a los Raptors, sólo ha podido mantenerse sano durante dos encuentros. Fue baja en el tercero y ahora se ha revelado que sufre una hinchazón en la rodilla izquierda. Se perderá un tiempo sin determinar, aunque se habla de varias semanas. Por suerte, la resonancia magnética a la que se ha sometido no ha mostrado daños estructurales, pero dados los antecedentes médicos de Kawhi, ya con 35 años, hay que ir con tiento. También los Timberwolves han recibido un duro golpe, pues se quedarán sin Anthony Edwards durante unos dos meses. El escolta se someterá a un procedimiento artroscópico en la rodilla derecha, que lleva tiempo dándole problemas. Los de Minnesota tenían muchas esperanzas depositadas en esta temporada, pero ven como se tuerce a las primeras de cambio. Además, Jaren Jackson Jr. comienza mal su etapa en los Jazz después de haber sufrido una rotura del ligamento colateral medial en su rodilla derecha. Aunque todo apunta a que no tendrá que pasar por el quirófano, deberá estar de baja entre seis y ocho semanas. Previamente a esas lesiones, la NBA ya había visto caer primero a Jalen Williams, que se dislocó el tobillo izquierdo y se fracturó el peroné en una acción espantosa, y a Cason Wallace, que se dañó el lábrum del hombro izquierdo. El primero no volverá a jugar este curso y el segundo se perderá unos cinco meses. Las aspiraciones de los Thunder, favoritos al anillo, han caído en picado tras esos dos duros varapalos. Además, se conocía también que Paolo Banquero, jugador franquicia de los Magic, estará entre cuatro y seis semanas de baja después de haber sufrido un esguince en el tobillo derecho.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards reportedly needs procedure on ailing right knee, expected to miss up to 2 months
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards needs an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and could miss up to two months, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards needs an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and could miss up to two months, ESPN's Shams Charania reports .

The precise nature of Edwards' injury wasn't clear from the report, but it's something that's bothered him since last season and through the start of the new campaign.

Edwards played through a chronic condition known as runner's knee in the playoffs last season. His production dipped as he also sustained a separate injury to his left knee that sidelined him for part a first-round series against the Nuggets. He returned to play in a second-round series loss to the Spurs, but wasn't himself.

Edwards focused on rest and healing in the offseason , but was visibly bothered by his right knee during the opening games of the regular season. He clutched his right knee in pain after a collision during a win over the Raptors on Sunday.

He was listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Cavaliers due to right knee injury management, but played 41 minutes in the game and scored 47 points. He was also initially listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Golden State Warriors that he will now miss.

The news is difficult blow for one of the game's brightest stars and a 3-1 Timberwolves team seeking to ascend to championship contention this season. Minnesota has advanced to the Western Conference finals in two of the last three seasons, but is seeking to break through to the NBA Finals with Edwards in his prime.

They restructured their roster around Edwards in the offseason, trading away mainstays Naz Reid and Julius Randle while acquiring All-Star point guard LaMelo Ball from the Charlotte Hornets.

Through four games, the revamped roster was paying dividends as Edwards thrived as a scorer alongside Ball's dynamic playmaking. Edwards was averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2 steals per game while shooting 40% on 11.3 3-point attempts per game in the new offense.

With Edwards and Ball leading the way, Minnesota's offense has been one of the most exciting in the league while scoring 122 points per game, the fourth-most in the NBA. Minnesota's average point differential of 17 points was the second-best in the league as of Tuesday.

Now the Timberwolves are looking at potentially playing the rest of of the calendar year without Edwards and left to hope that he's able to return from surgery at full force in time to compete for a playoff spot in the West.

In the meantime, Ball projects to take on a larger scoring role, and Ayo Dosunmu could be called into the starting lineup off the bench.

articles.title: Flavor Flav Hypes WNBA Finals Game 6 in Funny Post, Pushes for 'Paid Holiday' amid Schedule Changes
articles.summary: Flavor Flav wants basketball fans to take Thursday off in order to watch the matinee Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals off as their "contribution to gender equality."
articles.body:
Flavor Flav wants basketball fans to take Thursday off in order to watch the matinee Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals off as their "contribution to gender equality."

The rapper declared the day of Game 6 a "paid holiday" while sharing a template excuse letter in a Tuesday social media post.

"Dear boss... Everybody watches women's sports! You support women's sports, right?!" the note read. "So please go ahead and approve that day off."

Dream coach Karl Smesko said Monday when asked about the matinee game's timing that he would "like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games," per USA Today's Meghan L. Hall .

The date and time for the potentially championship-clinching game at State Farm Arena was finalized earlier this week after negotiations involving Atlanta Hawks and Cleveland Cavaliers games scheduled for Wednesday.

Dream ownership said in a Tuesday statement the game's midday Thursday tip-off "is not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for."

ESPN's Ramona Shelburne reported "the NBA and WNBA explored options to keep Game 6 in primetime" but settled for the matinee weekday due to the Hawks' and Cavaliers' schedules.

The move will allow the team to play in the 17,000-person arena in which the Dream will be playing next year rather than the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena in which Atlanta played this season.

The Valkyries could clinch the franchise's first title in Game 6 after claiming a 3-2 series lead with a Monday night 64-55 victory over the Atlanta Dream. Tip-off is scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Dream owners pen letter to fans after Game 6 rescheduling: 'Our concerns did not receive the attention they deserved'
articles.summary: The letter thanks fans for their support and gives more context on the WNBA Finals games that have been rescheduled.
articles.body:
The owners of the Atlanta Dream penned an open letter to the team's fans on Tuesday.

Owners Larry and Robyn Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery sent the letter addressing the controversial scheduling of Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. The game that could crown the Valkyries as champions won't be played in primetime, but instead will be in the middle of a workday at 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday.

While the letter begins by thanking fans, it states that ownership has long been aware of potential scheduling conflicts. It goes on to state that ownership raised those concerns, but they weren't addressed.

"Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena. "As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. "Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

"Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena.

"As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns.

"Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

The letter does not explicitly state who failed to address those concerns.

The scheduling problem stems from the fact that the Atlanta Dream play their regular-season games at Gateway Center Arena, which seats just 3,500 fans. In the playoffs, the Dream have been playing at State Farm Arena, the Atlanta Hawks' home venue that holds 17,000 fans.

The Dream already had to get creative with the scheduling of Games 3 and 4 because the Hawks had games at State Farm Arena on those dates. Atlanta moved Game 3 one day earlier, then played Game 4 as an early afternoon game on the weekend, leaving enough time to prepare for the Hawks' game later that night.

Game 6 is a similar situation. The Hawks have a game scheduled for Thursday night. State Farm Arena is open Friday night, but a potential Game 7, if needed, is scheduled for Saturday in San Francisco.

The WNBA didn't want its final two Finals games to be on back-to-back nights, so the only other option would have been to hold Game 7 eight days later, on Nov. 7.

To avoid that gap, a decision was made to hold Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday and tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET. The owners addressed this in the letter.

"Playing a midday game on a Thursday is not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for. And as much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage. That meant State Farm Arena."

They also shouted out the partners who helped reschedule the game.

"We are grateful to everyone who helped make that possible, especially our partners - the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena - who stepped up by adjusting their schedule on the fly, not once, but three times. And what a celebration it has been: a party, a concert and incredible Dream basketball all rolled into one."

Golden State leads the series 3-2 and can win the championship on Thursday.

The good news about this chaos is that, theoretically, it shouldn't happen again. The Dream have reached a deal with State Farm Arena, making it the team's home venue for all games beginning next year.

This likely means the schedule-makers will account for Hawks games when crafting the Dream schedule, and vice versa.

articles.title: Dream vs Valkyries Game 6 bumped from prime time to Thursday afternoon but WNBA stays silent on why

articles.body: The WNBA moved a potential championship-clinching game from Primetime to Thursday afternoon. Game 6 between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries will tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday at State Farm Arena, rather than its originally scheduled 8 p.m. start. OutKick asked Versant, USA Network’s parent company, what role it had in choosing or approving the new start time and whether it supported the move. And give Atlanta credit: Fans filled the larger building for Games 3 and 4. I previously questioned whether the Dream could fill State Farm Arena for the Finals, but they answered that with sellout crowds and a loud atmosphere. Of course, neither Game 3 nor Game 4 was played at a time when most adults are at work and most kids are in school. She also thanked the NBA, both teams, the Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for their collaboration and flexibility. articles.title: Ex-NBA Player Malik Beasley to Plead Guilty in Federal Sports Betting Case
articles.summary: Beasley is accused of manipulating his performance during NBA games to help others profit from sports betting
articles.body:
Malik Beasley is expected to plead guilty in a federal sports betting case, according to The Athletic

Federal prosecutors allege Beasley manipulated his performance during games while playing for the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2023-24 season

Beasley was indicted in June alongside five other men in an alleged scheme involving insider information and illegal bets

Former NBA player Malik Beasley is expected to plead guilty in a federal sports betting case months after prosecutors accused him of manipulating his performance during games while playing for the Milwaukee Bucks .

Beasley is scheduled to enter his guilty plea in Brooklyn federal court on Dec. 9, his attorney, Steve Haney, told The Athletic .

Beasley had been negotiating a plea agreement with federal prosecutors, and an overnight court docket notice indicated that he intended to plead guilty, according to ESPN . Beasley had not yet signed a plea agreement when Haney spoke with the outlet, the attorney said.

The case stems from allegations that Beasley, 29, manipulated his performance during some games in the 2023-24 NBA season and that others used information about his expected statistics to place bets, according to the U.S. Department of Justice 's June announcement of the athlete's indictment.

Beasley was indicted alongside former NBA player Edward Davis, NBA player agent Paolo Zamorano and three other men: William Brown, Robert Gorodetsky and Ernesto Plascencia, according to the Justice Department.

The defendants were charged with "wire fraud conspiracy, bribery in sporting contests, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, and money laundering conspiracy for their alleged roles in a scheme to bribe Beasley to manipulate his performance in NBA games and use inside information about Beasley's intended performance to profit via illegal betting activity," the Justice Department said in a news release at the time.

Federal authorities alleged that Beasley told Davis on several occasions that he planned to underperform in upcoming games. Davis allegedly passed that information to co-conspirators, who then placed bets on Beasley's statistics, according to the indictment.

One example cited by prosecutors involved a Jan. 26, 2024, game against the Cleveland Cavaliers . Beasley allegedly told Davis that he planned to record fewer rebounds than expected. Beasley finished the game with three rebounds, one below his betting line, according to the indictment.

"In total, the defendants and their co-conspirators placed fraudulent wagers totaling hundreds of thousands of dollars conditioned on Beasley's fixed performance in the influenced games at issue via multiple betting operators," the Justice Department alleged.

"As alleged, the defendants turned professional basketball into a criminal betting operation, bribing then-NBA player Malik Beasley to fix his performance in multiple games in order to place fraudulent wagers, enrich themselves and cheat legitimate sportsbooks," Joseph Nocella Jr., the U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of New York, said in a statement .

"Bribery and insider betting schemes like this one involving former NBA players and a current NBA player agent who exploited inside NBA information for profit erode the integrity of American sports and victimize the sports-watching public," Nocella added.

Following the indictment in June, Haney issued a statement to PEOPLE urging the public to reserve judgment until all the facts were known.

"An indictment is nothing but a probable cause one-sided charging document," Haney said. "It is not evidence and Malik maintains his presumption of innocence throughout this two year investigation. We ask that people reserve judgment until all the facts are known."

Beasley played for six NBA teams over a nine-year career. He last played in the NBA during the 2024-25 season with the Detroit Pistons and also played 17 games for Santurce in Puerto Rico's Baloncesto Superior Nacional last season.

PEOPLE has reached out to Haney and a representative for Beasley for comment.

NBA icon Dominique Wilkins is stepping into a new role at the collegiate level.

The Hall of Famer was named the new college basketball general manager at Alabama State on Tuesday ahead of the start of the Hornets' season next week.

Wilkins' involvement in Alabama State's basketball program is perhaps a bit unexpected since he played collegiately at Georgia and isn't from Alabama. Nonetheless, it's an exciting moment for the SWAC program.

It's hard to say how much of a role Wilkins will play for Alabama State on a daily basis, but having a legendary name attached to the program should generate some more excitement and recruiting interest for the school.

The Hornets have appeared in the NCAA tournament six times, winning their first game, a First Four game against Saint Francis, in 2025. Alabama State has won the SWAC Tournament five times, with its most recent win coming in 2025.

Tony Madlock was the Hornets' coach from 2022 to 2026 but stepped down at the end of last season after a 10-22 campaign, taking over as the associate head coach of Memphis.

Alabama State hired veteran head coach Chris Wright ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and he'll look to get the Hornets back to the NCAA tournament early on in his tenure. Wright was most recently the head coach of Langston, an NAIA school in Oklahoma.

Alabama State will begin its first season with Wright at the helm and Wilkins in the front office next Tuesday when it faces Texas A&M.

articles.title: John Wall Shares Heartfelt Story About His Late Mother
articles.summary: Former Washington Wizards star John Wall revealed a heartfelt story about his late mother, Frances Pulley, who passed away in 2019 at age 58.Pulley passed aw...
articles.body:
Former Washington Wizards star John Wall revealed a heartfelt story about his late mother, Frances Pulley, who passed away in 2019 at age 58.

Pulley passed away on December 13, 2019, after a courageous battle with breast cancer.

Nearly seven years after his mother passed away, Wall reveals that he still texts his mother every day.

Speaking in a new interview, Wall revealed his touching story about texting his mother on a daily basis.

"I made sure I paid the bill for that for the rest of the time I'm going to be on this earth, so I can send my daily text in the morning and my daily text at night. It helps me. I know she can't respond, but I can still send my messages and know that nobody else has her number. And sometimes you have your moments when you just sitting at home and you just reflect. And I always look at pictures and reflect. My display screen on my phone is my first game against the Sixers, and we win the game and I give her a hug, and I always keep that as my bio picture," Wall said.

Wall was drafted by the Washington Wizards with the first overall pick in the 2010 NBA Draft out of Kentucky.

He spent the first nine seasons of his NBA career with the Wizards before pit stops with the Houston Rockets and Los Angeles Clippers to close out his career. He last played in the NBA in 2023 for the Clippers.

In 647 career regular-season NBA games, Wall averaged 18.7 points with 4.2 rebounds and 8.9 assists per game.

Wall finished second in Rookie of the Year voting in 2010, just behind Blake Griffin . He was named an All-Star four times during his NBA career and was also named to the Third All-NBA Team in 2017.

Overall, Wall had an excellent NBA career even though it got cut short at the end.

Wall, who is now 36 years old, is the president of basketball operations at Howard University. He also works as a Wizards analyst for Monumental Sports Network.

articles.title: Natalie Nakase's ‘extremist' style hit a wall in WNBA Finals. Then the Valkyries coach evolved
articles.summary: After Natalie Nakase gave herself an "F-minus" for the first three games of the WNBA Finals, she learned, listened and adjusted. Now the coach has the Golden...
articles.body:
Natalie Nakase finished discussing how her Golden State Valkyries are one win from a championship and stepped out of the news conference room. Waiting in the hallway was NBA legend Chris Paul. She and Paul walked toward the Valkyries locker room, their heads bent together, deep in conversation.

Nakase is heading into uncharted territory for the WNBA. There has never been a Game 6 - or a Game 7 if it comes to that - in league history. Many of the coaches, who come to the league from the college ranks or as WNBA assistants, are unfamiliar with the rigors of a seven-game series.

But Nakase, who earned her coaching chops with the Los Angeles Clippers, can draw on her NBA background and her NBA mentors to help her navigate through this long and intense WNBA Finals.

"As boring as it sounds, it's staying healthy, maintaining high energy," Nakase said. "Rest and recovery. You know the Clippers had injuries (in the playoffs). And last year, too. I learned my lesson. We were injured. … Stay consistent, block out the noise, understand the game plan."

What Nakase learned during her time with the Clippers - where she began as a video coordinator and worked up to an assistant coach under both Doc Rivers and Tyronn Lue - is that seven-game series are long. There is time to adjust. One bad game doesn't signal doom. Even two consecutive losses don't define a series.

"That's the beauty of a seven-game series, it is long," Nakase said. "We keep our habits the same, control what we can control. Don't overreact."

It's been fascinating watching Nakase grow into her role as a head coach, on the big stage. One part of her is an intensely competitive, detail-obsessed and driven coach, who plays war sounds during practice, calls her players "killers," prefers salty language and insists she needs "no joy" to motivate her - "just winning." Who forgets to eat and goes so hard that she collapsed to the ground during the late minutes of a deciding game against Dallas.

She learned that demeanor from her late father Gary, who pushed her relentlessly. Her father didn't easily offer praise or affection.

"Basketball was his love language," she said. "It was discipline and it was time. He was there every single step of the way."

Gary always made the youngest of his three daughters - Natalie jokes that she was supposed to be Nathan - play with older kids or with boys, so that she would be the worst on her teams and always had to fight to get better.

"He instilled in me life lessons, hard lessons," she said. "He loved to throw adversity my way."

It made his youngest daughter tough. She took that toughness to UCLA, where she walked on and became the starting point guard. She took it to Germany and Japan, where she first played, then learned to coach. She took it to the NBA, where she started at the bottom.

When she joined the WNBA in 2022, as Becky Hammon's top assistant in Las Vegas, her players thought of her as the "strict coach." The serious coach. No room, as Tiffany Hayes said, "for playing around."

But now, as the head coach of a group of connected women, Nakase has grown and evolved.

"I think my identity changes from year to year," she said. "I'm a constant learner. I love to ask questions. I have a curious mindset."

One of the things she learned last year was about health. Her team suffered key injuries late in the season, to Hayes and Kayla Thornton among others. Nakase took responsibility, feeling like her practices may have been too intensive.

"It motivated me to be organized and intentional on off-days," she said. "I also wanted to make sure all 14 (on the roster) can be two-way players. If they weren't high-level two-way players I wanted to develop them because we play so hard. So there was intentionality around the kind of players we had and then seeing what they did in the offseason. Seeing how much rest they needed. Everything was calculated."

Her NBA mentors have also helped her grow and evolve. She said that Paul, during these playoffs, has counseled her to instill confidence in the players. To be there for them when they're low. To stay connected during the sticky times.

Former Clippers assistant Armond Hill, who has been a regular presence around the Valkyries during this playoff run, calls Nakase "grasshopper" and tries to calm her down, telling her to remember to breathe.

"I want to do everything right," Nakase said. "I'm a perfectionist. I'm an extremist. He says, 'Just take a breath. Make sure you're clear and concise with your game plan. Try not to get everything done all in one night.'"

During these playoffs Nakase has spoken a lot about vulnerability. The importance of her players being vulnerable with her, and of her being open and honest with them. She is revealing her softer side, talking regularly about love and care and meaningful communication.

"Part of my DNA is an obsession extremist, it's why I want to win everything so quickly," she said this week, when addressing what she felt she did wrong earlier in these Finals. "That's not really what will work in a long series. It's delivering my message a little bit slower, a little more clear. … It's always on me. It's always on the head coach's delivery."

What exactly, Nakase was asked late Monday night after the Valkyries had taken a 3-2 lead in the series, is an obsession extremist?

"I'm an extremist because I can keep doing the same thing over and over again until I perfect it," she said. "That's probably why I felt I could perfect the perfect game plan and win it right away.

"I had to listen to my players, like Kiah Stokes , who said 'It's a long series coach, take a breath.' Listen to my mentors who said 'It's going to be a battle, why don't you just take a beat' … I was hazy at times. I give myself an F-minus for Games 1, 2 and 3. My communication was poor.

"Sometimes extremist doesn't work well in a seven-game series."

Nakase is not getting an F-minus anymore. She is evolving as a head coach before our eyes. Learning. Listening. Adjusting. And now, in just their second year of existence, the Valkyries are on the brink of history, one win away from a championship.

That's pretty extreme, in all the best ways.

articles.standfirst: El base mete 41 y es el sexto jugador de la franquicia angelina con 20 o más actuaciones por encima de la cuarentena
articles.summary: El base mete 41 y es el sexto jugador de la franquicia angelina con 20 o más actuaciones por encima de la cuarentena
articles.body: La primera derrota de los Lakers esta temporada después de arrancar con tres victorias llegó pese a otro recital anotador de Luka Doncic. Perdieron ante los Blazers por 129-136 pese a los 41 puntos del base, que acumula 93 en los dos últimos encuentros. Con esta actuación, suma ya 20 partidos por encima de la cuarentena con la franquicia angelina. Es el sexto jugador que alcanza esa cifra. Sus cinco compañeros en la lista son mitos que vivieron muchas temporadas en el equipo: Kobe Byant, Elgin Baylor, Jerry West, Shaquille O'Neal y George Mikan. Doncic no hace ni dos años que llegó a Los Ángeles. La racha de los Lakers la truncaron entre Ja Morant, Deni Avdija, Damian Lillard y Jrue Holiday. Todos metieron al menos 20 puntos, con los dos primeros llegando a un máximo de 23, para mantener a los Blazers invictos después de los tres primeros encuentros, algo que es la segunda vez que viven en 15 años. Portland amasó 10 puntos de ventaja al inicio del último periodo (106-116). Doncic salió desde el banquillo para liderar la remontada. Los Lakers llegaron a igualar a 120, pero el acierto exterior de los Blazers volvió a darles ventaja. Holiday, Lillard y Avdija metieron sendos triples. El esloveno y Ziaire Williams intentaban dar réplica. Los visitantes encontraron otro argumento postrero en Morant, que anotó dos canastas seguidas. El golpe definitivo lo ejecutó Lillard, que demostró que su grave lesión en el tendón de Aquiles no le ha hecho perder puntualidad cuando el partido se calienta. A falta de 43 segundos, clavaba el triple que fijaba el marcador final y abría una distancia ya definitiva. Doncic anotó 16 de sus puntos en el primer cuarto, se mostró intenso en defensa y repartió también nueve asistencias. Su mejor escudero fue una vez más Austin Reaves, que metió 26 puntos. Walker Kessler sumó 13 y ocho rebotes y Sandro Mamukelashvili añadió 17, 13 de ellos antes del descanso.
